cycle7-git-procedure-AMENDED (SUPERSEDES the blanket 'never git add'; verified by BOTH sessions on git 2.32.0.windows.1). The blanket rule was WRONG and impossible to follow: git commit --only -- <path> FAILS OUTRIGHT on an untracked file with "error: pathspec ... did not match any file(s) known to git", and git commit --include reports "nothing added to commit but untracked files present". --only can only restrict a commit to paths git already knows about, and every new report/evidence/test file is untracked at commit time. BINDING PROCEDURE: (1) MODIFYING a tracked file -- git commit --only -F <msgfile> -- <exact path>, no staging at any point. (2) CREATING a new file -- git add is unavoidable, so minimise the window: run 'git status --porcelain' (index must be empty), then 'git add -- <exact path> && git commit --only -F <msgfile> -- <exact path>' as a SINGLE shell invocation, then 'git status --porcelain' again (index must be empty). Keeping --only pins the commit to that one path so even if a third crew stages something inside the window it cannot ride along. This collapses exposure to microseconds rather than eliminating it -- the best available, and strictly better than the bare-add-then-later-bare-commit pattern that bit us twice. (3) STILL ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN: git add -A, git add ., git add -u, git commit -a, and any git add not immediately followed by its own scoped commit in the same invocation.
